result.title: A Stevens's Power Law Check-up of GPT-5.5's Image-Based Visualization Reading
result.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, including supplementary material. Accepted by the VISxGenAI workshop at IEEE VIS 2026
result.summary: We adapt Stevens's power law to measure the innate ability of AI models to read visualizations, which can reveal the built-in perceptual mechanisms of algorithmic models. In our pilot study, models see no legend. A model first views a reference visual representation and estimates its magnitude, then estimates the magnitude of each subsequent image of the same representation relative to that reference. Our evaluation of twelve visual variables makes how algorithmic models read visual encodings measurable, comparable with human perception, and more interpretable to humans.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作借用 Stevens 幂律，让模型先看一个参照可视化并估计其量值，再对同表示的后续图像做相对量值估计，从而测量十二种视觉变量的读取能力，使算法模型的视觉编码读取可与人感知比较。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「参照—相对判断」范式可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与内部视觉细节保留提供可核查的探测手段，但该文聚焦感知量值估计而非 latent 推理状态，联系仍较间接。
